{

    "Treat the project as Spring XD (a Spring ecosystem project) built with Gradle, mixing Java, Scala, and supporting Spark/Kafka integrations.",
    "Reuse the existing Spring XD module system and build infrastructure rather than introducing new frameworks.",
    "For U1, implement deployment tooling as a Gradle task / shell wrapper that mirrors existing module deployment conventions.",
    "For U2, author content in the project's wiki (Confluence or Markdown wiki) following the existing 'Troubleshooting' section style.",

    "For U5, refactor publish-maven.gradle to read versions from dependencies.properties using a Gradle Properties loader, keeping backward compatibility for existing values.",
    "For U7, perform a one-pass sonar review: fix the small/medium violations directly and mark the rest as 'Won't Fix' or 'False Positive' with justification in the SonarQube UI.",
    "For U8, build the sample as a runnable Spring XD batch job that wraps a Spark job, including a README with run instructions and an integration test stub.",
    "Reuse the existing CI infrastructure to validate changes; add or update CI jobs only where strictly required (e.g., external Kafka)."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The developer is already familiar with Spring XD, Gradle, Scala, Spark, and Kafka; no ramp-up training is included.",
    "A working development environment, build tooling, IDE, Wiki access, and SonarQube access are already available.",

    "Code review and minor CI adjustments are folded into the activity estimates rather than tracked separately.",
    "U4 and U6 share substantial implementation work but are still estimated as two separate activities to honor the user-story split."
  ],

      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Requirements analysis and technical design",
      "activity_description": "Review the 8 user stories, explore the Spring XD codebase, confirm the affected modules, and produce a short technical design covering file changes, build changes, and test impacts.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Spark streaming module deployment tooling for Scala (U1)",
      "activity_description": "Implement and document a deployment entry point that allows a Spark streaming module written in Scala to be packaged and submitted like existing Java modules; include a small Scala sample and a Gradle deploy task.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },

      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Wiki documentation for recommended ulimit (U2)",
      "activity_description": "Add a 'Troubleshooting' section to the XD wiki describing the 10K ulimit recommendation, the underlying Too-many-open-files symptom, and steps to raise the limit on common OSes.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Add date to container log pattern (U3)",
      "activity_description": "Update xd-container-logger.properties so the log layout includes a date/time token; verify the change in a local container run and in a sample log file.",
      "most_likely_effort": 2
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Refactor Kafka tests to use a separate broker process (U4)",
      "activity_description": "Update the Kafka test harness to start the broker in a separate JVM process controllable via a build flag, decoupling it from the test runner for faster and more stable local builds.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Refactor publish-maven.gradle to use dependencies.properties (U5)",
      "activity_description": "Read Spring Boot, hadoop-common, and other dependency versions from a central dependencies.properties file; verify that the published POMs still resolve and that the local publish path works.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Run Kafka tests against an external broker (U6)",
      "activity_description": "Enable an 'external broker' mode for Kafka integration tests, document how to point the build at a running broker, and update CI to use this mode to reduce build footprint.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Sonar violations review and remediation (U7)",
      "activity_description": "Triage the current SonarQube violations: fix relevant issues directly in code and mark irrelevant ones as 'Won't Fix' or 'False Positive' with justification in SonarQube.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Spark batch job sample (U8)",
      "activity_description": "Develop a runnable Spring XD batch job that drives a Spark job to demonstrate distributed computation; add a README, run script, and a lightweight integration test.",
      "most_likely_effort": 14
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Integration testing and build verification",
      "activity_description": "Run the full Gradle build with the new external-Kafka mode, execute the Spark sample, and confirm all user stories behave end-to-end; capture any regressions.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Release notes, wiki updates, and final cleanup",

    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 80
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Treat the project as Spring XD (a Spring ecosystem project) built with Gradle, mixing Java, Scala, and supporting Spark/Kafka integrations.
Reuse the existing Spring XD module system and build infrastructure rather than introducing new frameworks.
For U1, implement deployment tooling as a Gradle task / shell wrapper that mirrors existing module deployment conventions.
For U2, author content in the project's wiki (Confluence or Markdown wiki) following the existing 'Troubleshooting' section style.
For U3, modify the existing xd-container-logger.properties log pattern to include the date token (e.g. %d) instead of restructuring the logging stack.

For U4 and U6, refactor the Kafka test harness so an embedded broker is replaced by a lifecycle-managed external broker process, configurable via build flags; the two stories are implemented as a single coherent refactor but estimated separately per the user-story scope.
For U5, refactor publish-maven.gradle to read versions from dependencies.properties using a Gradle Properties loader, keeping backward compatibility for existing values.
For U7, perform a one-pass sonar review: fix the small/medium violations directly and mark the rest as 'Won't Fix' or 'False Positive' with justification in the SonarQube UI.
For U8, build the sample as a runnable Spring XD batch job that wraps a Spark job, including a README with run instructions and an integration test stub.
Reuse the existing CI infrastructure to validate changes; add or update CI jobs only where strictly required (e.g., external Kafka).
assumptions: The developer is already familiar with Spring XD, Gradle, Scala, Spark, and Kafka; no ramp-up training is included.
A working development environment, build tooling, IDE, Wiki access, and SonarQube access are already available.
Java 8 is the target JDK for Spring XD (consistent with the 1.1.0 SNAPSHOT era in the spec).
An external Kafka broker can be started on localhost for tests; no remote broker provisioning is required.
SonarQube has already been run on the codebase; the 'current violations' exist and just need review/fix.
Sample Spark batch job is intended for demonstration only and does not need to be production-hardened.
The Maven Central / Spring repository is reachable from the build environment to publish artifacts.
Code review and minor CI adjustments are folded into the activity estimates rather than tracked separately.
U4 and U6 share substantial implementation work but are still estimated as two separate activities to honor the user-story split.
